subject: physiology
title: Deglutition, Lower Oesophageal Sphincter, and Gastric Emptying

steps.tx: Swallowing, or deglutition, is a complex neuromuscular reflex coordinated by the brainstem deglutition centre within the medulla oblongata. It is divided chronologically into three phases: the voluntary oral phase, the involuntary **pharyngeal phase of swallowing**, and the involuntary oesophageal phase.
steps.say: Deglutition is coordinated by the medullary swallowing centre, progressing through oral, pharyngeal, and oesophageal phases.

nodes.label: Voluntary Oral Phase: Tongue Pushes Food Bolus Posteriorly into Oropharynx
Involuntary Pharyngeal Phase: Soft Palate Elevates, Epiglottis Closes Larynx
Upper Oesophageal Sphincter (Cricopharyngeus) Relaxes; Bolus Enters Oesophagus
Involuntary Oesophageal Phase: Primary Peristaltic Wave Propels Bolus to Stomach

steps.tx: During the pharyngeal phase, respiration is momentarily arrested for one to two seconds by inhibitory reflexes in the medullary respiratory center, known as deglutition apnoea. Simultaneously, the soft palate elevates to close the posterior nares, the vocal cords adduct, and the larynx moves upward under the epiglottis, preventing **pulmonary food aspiration**.
steps.say: During swallowing, respiration stops and the larynx closes upward under the epiglottis to protect airways from aspiration.

left.title: Pharyngeal Protection Mechanisms
points: Elevation of soft palate seals off nasopharynx
True and false vocal cords close tightly
Larynx pulled upward and forward by suprahyoid muscles
Epiglottis swings downward over laryngeal inlet

right.title: Neuromuscular Coordination
points: Sensory afferents via trigeminal, glossopharyngeal, vagus nerves
Medullary swallowing center in nucleus tractus solitarius
Deglutition apnoea halts respiratory ramp firing
Cricopharyngeus muscle relaxes to open upper sphincter

steps.tx: Food propulsion through the thoracic oesophagus is driven by primary peristalsis, a continuous aborally moving contraction wave traveling at two to four centimetres per second. If a large or sticky food bolus lodges within the lumen, local distension triggers enteric sensory afferents, eliciting **secondary peristalsis**.
steps.say: Primary peristalsis sweeps swallowed food down the oesophagus, while secondary peristalsis clears any remaining lodged bolus.

left.title: Primary Peristalsis
points: Triggered by swallowing act in pharynx
Coordinated centrally by vagal swallowing center
Takes 8 to 10 seconds to traverse entire oesophagus
Persists even if bolus is purely liquid or negligible

right.title: Secondary Peristalsis
points: Triggered locally by retained food or acid reflux distension
Mediated through local enteric nerve plexuses and vagovagal arcs
Repeats continuously until oesophageal lumen is fully cleared
Essential protective clearance mechanism in acid reflux

steps.tx: The distal boundary between the oesophagus and stomach is maintained by the **lower oesophageal sphincter**, a three-centimetre specialized zone of tonically contracted circular smooth muscle. Baseline tone generates resting pressures between fifteen and thirty millimetres of mercury, preventing caustic retrograde reflux of gastric contents.
steps.say: The lower oesophageal sphincter maintains resting pressure of fifteen to thirty millimetres of mercury to prevent gastric reflux.

cols: Effect on Lower Oesophageal Sphincter Tone

steps.tx: Autoimmune destruction of inhibitory nitric oxide-producing and VIP-producing ganglion cells in the myenteric plexus causes **esophageal achalasia**. Lacking receptive relaxation, the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to open during swallowing, leading to massive proximal oesophageal dilation, progressive dysphagia for solids and liquids, and regurgitation.
steps.say: Achalasia results from loss of myenteric inhibitory neurons, preventing the lower sphincter from relaxing during swallowing.

vis.caption: Aperistalsis of oesophageal body, failure of lower sphincter relaxation, and bird-beak tapering in achalasia.

steps.tx: Upon arrival of a food bolus, the proximal stomach undergoes **adaptive gastric relaxation**, expanding its internal volume from fifty millilitres up to fifteen hundred millilitres with virtually no elevation in intragastric pressure. This vagally mediated reflex is abolished by bilateral surgical vagotomy.
steps.say: Adaptive gastric relaxation allows the stomach to hold over a litre of food without increasing internal pressure.

Vagovagal Reflex Arc Projects to Brainstem Nucleus Tractus Solitarius
Vagal Postganglionic Inhibitory Neurons Release Nitric Oxide and VIP
Gastric Fundus and Body Receptively Relax to Accommodate up to 1.5 Litres

steps.tx: Mechanical breakdown and sieving of gastric contents is regulated by **antral retropulsion**. Vigorous peristaltic waves sweep toward the closed pyloric sphincter, crushing solid particles against the terminal antrum and retropelling them backward until chyme is liquefied to particles smaller than two millimetres.
steps.say: Antral retropulsion crushes solid food against the closed pyloric sphincter until it is reduced to particles under two millimetres.

left.title: Gastric Emptying of Liquids
points: Governed by proximal stomach tonic contractions
Follows rapid exponential emptying kinetics
Isotonic saline empties faster than nutrient-dense broths
Rapidly enters duodenum within 30 to 60 minutes

right.title: Gastric Emptying of Solids
points: Requires mechanical antral milling and retropulsion
Follows linear zero-order emptying kinetics after lag phase
Only particles < 2 mm pass through pyloric sphincter
Lipids and acidic chyme potently delay emptying via CCK and secretin

steps.tx: Between meals the gut runs a cleaning cycle most people never feel. The **migrating motor complex** sweeps strong contractions from stomach to ileum every ninety minutes or so, clearing debris and bacteria that fasting leaves behind. Eating interrupts it instantly, which is one cost of constant grazing. Its failure contributes to bacterial overgrowth, bloating and the nausea investigated with motility studies.
steps.say: The migrating motor complex sweeps the fasting gut every ninety minutes, clearing debris and bacteria. Eating interrupts the cycle at once.

vis.alt: Image showing the migrating motor complex sweeping contractions through the fasting gut.
vis.caption: A wave of contraction is shown travelling from stomach down the small bowel. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: During the interdigestive fasting state, the stomach and small intestine clear indigestible debris via the **migrating motor complex**. Mediated by cyclical surges of the duodenal hormone motilin every ninety minutes, these intense peristaltic housekeeping waves sweep through the gastrointestinal tract, preventing small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.
steps.say: The migrating motor complex acts as a periodic fasting housekeeping wave, clearing debris to prevent bacterial overgrowth.
